FLEX Migration Strategy Guide

From Legacy OSPC to AI-Ready Open Cloud

Still on Legacy OSPC? Move to FLEX and Unlock Your AI-Ready Cloud Future.

Before any migration starts, customers need one clear business answer: who should move, why it matters, and when to move. FLEX gives OSPC customers a modern open-cloud foundation with better performance, lower TCO, Kubernetes readiness, OpenCenter modernization, and makes your Business System ready for AI-Power Up.

💡
Why move?

Lower TCO, fewer VMware and hyperscaler surprises, stronger performance, and a safer path to growth.

🎯
Who should move?

Customers with critical OSPC, VMware, private cloud, or hyperscaler workloads needing control and cost clarity.

⚡
What moves?

VMs, apps, data, images, networks, security rules, sovereignty controls, and operations move into FLEX.

⏰
When to move?

When OSPC ages, VMware renewals hurt, hyperscaler spend grows, sovereignty matters, or disruption risk is too high.

🎯

Who Should Move to FLEX?

Ideal Customer Profile

FLEX is ideal for customers ready to modernize beyond legacy OSPC, VMware cost pressure, or hyperscaler complexity without losing openness, control, data sovereignty, and enterprise-grade operations. The best candidates are customers who:

✓ Run important production workloads on legacy OSPC, VMware, private cloud, or hyperscaler platforms.
✓ Need better performance, scalability, availability, and predictable infrastructure outcomes.
✓ Want to reduce long-term cost, VMware licensing exposure, hyperscaler bill shock, and vendor lock-in.
✓ Planning AI, Kubernetes, analytics, sovereign cloud, or modern application platforms.
✓ Need hybrid cloud flexibility across public, private, dedicated, regulated, or data-sovereign environments.
✓ Want a phased migration path from OSPC, VMware, or hyperscaler estates instead of a risky big-bang cutover.
✓ Require enterprise-grade support, security, compliance alignment, data residency, and operational expertise.

FLEX is for customers who want to lower up to 3x their current TCO, regain control from VMware or hyperscaler lock-in, protect data sovereignty, and improve business system performance, resiliency, and security — to grow their business revenue.

💡

Why Move to FLEX?

Business Value & TCO

The move to FLEX is not only a technical upgrade. It is a business opportunity to escape VMware renewal pressure, reduce hyperscaler cost volatility, protect data sovereignty, and deliver better performance with lower operational friction.

What Moves to FLEX?

Modernization Scope

FLEX is not just a landing zone for virtual machines. It is the next operating foundation for business systems leaving legacy OSPC, VMware estates, or hyperscaler sprawl while improving cost control, sovereignty, network governance, security posture, and automation.

Move the Workloads That Matter

Business Systems ERP, CRM, commerce, portals, regulated apps, and revenue systems.
Application Tiers Web, API, middleware, worker, VMware VM, and cloud-native services.
Data Foundations Databases, files, object data, backups, sync plans, and data residency rules.
Cloud Controls Images, flavors, networks, security groups, IPs, access, and sovereignty controls.
Outcome

A cleaner, faster, future-ready platform.

The migration captures what exists, maps what must change, and lands each workload on FLEX with right sizing, network design, governance, sovereignty, and validation.

01Discover application dependency, business criticality, and current platform cost drivers.
02Map compute, storage, network, security, sovereignty, and cutover requirements.
03Validate performance, resiliency, access, compliance, and rollback readiness.
From

Legacy OSPC patterns, VMware renewal pressure, hyperscaler sprawl, aging images, fixed designs, and infrastructure constraints.

Through

Discovery, assessment, right-sizing, cost modeling, migration waves, sovereignty mapping, UAT, staged cutover, and rollback planning.

To

Modern OpenStack services, better economics, stronger automation, data control, and a cloud foundation ready for AI and Kubernetes.

The WHAT is the customer’s complete operating footprint: workloads, data, controls, sovereignty, and confidence needed to keep the business moving while the platform becomes stronger.

⏰

When Should Customers Move to FLEX?

Migration Triggers

Customers should consider moving when one or more OSPC, VMware, hyperscaler, sovereignty, or modernization triggers appear:

1
Current platform limits performance or scalability

OSPC ages, VMware clusters constrain capacity, or hyperscaler architecture becomes too complex.

2
Infrastructure cost needs optimization

VMware renewal costs rise, hyperscaler bills become unpredictable, or utilization needs improvement.

3
New projects are being launched

AI pilots, Kubernetes, analytics, sovereign cloud, or modernization programs should start on FLEX directly.

4
Reduce migration risk with phased move

FLEX supports discover → assess → migrate → validate → cut over from OSPC, VMware, or hyperscaler estates. No big-bang required.

5
Need a future-ready cloud foundation

Hybrid cloud, open-source flexibility, data sovereignty, or long-term workload portability — FLEX is the right platform to evaluate now.

Migration Trigger Conditions

Technical and business conditions driving migration from OSPC, VMware, hyperscaler, or legacy environments to FLEX.

Condition / trigger Why it matters Example use case
Need for modern, OpenStack-based infrastructure FLEX runs on current-generation OpenStack with newer APIs, better automation, and open cloud standards, giving customers an alternative to aging OSPC, VMware dependency, or hyperscaler-only operating models. A company operating legacy apps on OSPC and VMware wants Terraform and Kubernetes-friendly automation without moving every workload into a hyperscaler account.
Desire for more flexible networking and segmentation FLEX supports modern segmentation, tenant isolation, floating IPs, and network governance without forcing customers into complex hyperscaler networking or rigid legacy designs. An e-commerce platform needs isolated PCI, analytics, and internal application networks while avoiding hyperscaler networking sprawl and data egress exposure.
Need to import custom images or use vendor images FLEX supports custom images and common vendor images, helping customers migrate VMware VM patterns, OSPC images, or hyperscaler-built workloads into a controlled open platform. A DevOps team wants to move hardened Linux and Windows images out of VMware or a hyperscaler into FLEX while preserving security baselines and operational consistency.
Scaling beyond legacy limits or regions FLEX provides scalable capacity and modern hardware when OSPC is constrained, VMware clusters are expensive to expand, or hyperscaler growth is creating runaway spend. A SaaS provider needs regional growth but wants predictable economics, less licensing exposure, and fewer hyperscaler egress surprises.
Push toward cost-efficient, license-free infrastructure FLEX helps reduce proprietary virtualization exposure, hyperscaler bill volatility, and lock-in by using an open-source-based private cloud model. A financial services firm wants to reduce VMware renewal pressure and repatriate steady-state cloud workloads from a hyperscaler into managed open infrastructure.
Requirement for advanced automation and CI/CD pipelines FLEX integrates with Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, and GitOps workflows while avoiding brittle legacy tooling and hyperscaler-specific automation lock-in. A platform team wants consistent pipelines across VMware exits, OSPC migrations, and selected hyperscaler repatriation workloads.
Compliance, security, or data sovereignty upgrade FLEX supports stronger segmentation, isolation, and data placement control for customers facing sovereignty, residency, regulated workload, or hyperscaler data-control concerns. A healthcare or public-sector organization needs data residency, isolation, and compliance alignment that is harder to prove across sprawling hyperscaler accounts.
Long-term roadmap and platform exit strategy FLEX gives customers a managed modernization path for OSPC migration, VMware exit planning, hyperscaler repatriation, or hybrid cloud rebalancing. A customer phases legacy WebLogic, VMware-hosted apps, and steady-state hyperscaler workloads into FLEX over several migration waves.

Stage 1 — Discovery & Assessment

Scan, analyze, and plan the migration scope

  • Run OSPC Infrastructure Scanner to inventory VMs
  • Scan networks, volumes, security groups, LBs
  • Define Business Systems with Business System Templates
  • App Dependency & Service Comparison analysis
  • Performance baseline (CPU, RAM, IOPS, network)

YT Stage 1: OSPC Scanner & Assessment Guide (12 min)

Stage 2 — Migrations

VM Snapshot, DB Replication, Infra Clone, K8s

  • Full Business System Migration — orchestrate all components
  • Linux/Windows VM Snapshot & Volume Migration
  • App & Database Replication (MySQL, Postgres, MongoDB)
  • Infra Clone: networks, subnets, security groups, LBs
  • APPs Containerization with architecture templates

Stage 2b/2c — Cost & Performance

TCO comparison and performance baseline on FLEX

  • Compare OSPC vs FLEX monthly cost per VM
  • TCO savings projection over 1, 3, 5 years
  • Post-migration performance benchmarking
  • Flavor right-sizing recommendations
  • Identify over-provisioned vs under-provisioned resources

YT TCO Analysis & Performance Gain on FLEX (9 min)

Stage 3 — Validation & UAT

Business-System-Aware testing and validation

  • Server target comparison (OSPC vs FLEX side-by-side)
  • Business system component health checks
  • Database comparison queries (SELECT 1, row counts)
  • Application endpoint smoke tests (HTTP health)
  • Performance readiness gate before cutover

Stage 4 — Cutover & Traffic Transition

DNS switch, traffic redirect, go-live coordination

  • Cutover checklist with owner assignments
  • DNS record updates and TTL management
  • Traffic transition (blue/green, weighted routing)
  • Business system cutover sequencing
  • Rollback plan with one-click revert

Stages 5–8 — Operations & Modernization

Stabilize → IaC → GitOps → AIOps

  • Stage 6: IaC, Backup, Disaster Recovery, Restore testing
  • Stage 7: GitOps, OpenCenter Modernization, CI/CD
  • Stage 8: AIOps, predictive scaling, continuous operations

Category FLEX Ready app stacks Why FLEX Ready Not Yet FLEX Ready app stacks Why not yet FLEX Ready
Open-source web appsWordPress, Drupal, Magento, Laravel, Django, Flask, Node.js web appsStandard Linux runtimes, portable app/data tiers, easy VM or app-tier rebuildVery old PHP/Apache apps tied to obsolete OS or local legacy modulesOld runtime, unsupported packages, hidden dependencies
Standard 3-tier business appsWeb + API + DB on supported Linux/WindowsClean separation of app and data tiers, easier rehost or replatformMonolith with app + DB + files + scheduler all on one VMTight coupling, hardcoded paths, embedded dependencies

Standard Windows business appsWindows Server 2019/2022 app servers, IIS apps, .NET-supported appsModern OS, portable workloads, easier rebuild on FLEX VMsWindows 2003/2008 legacy apps, old IIS/.NET dependenciesUnsupported OS, security risk, migration blockers
Linux application tiersUbuntu 20.04/22.04/24.04, RHEL 8/9, Rocky, AlmaLinux, Debian 11/12Supported guest OS, predictable package ecosystemRHEL/CentOS 5/6, Ubuntu 14/16, old Debian, old custom kernelsLegacy kernel/userspace, driver and package issues
API / middleware tiersJava app servers, Tomcat, Spring Boot, Nginx, HAProxy, RabbitMQ, modern middlewareUsually portable if config and connectivity are understoodMiddleware requiring old libraries, old JVM, legacy init scripts, appliance-like packagingRuntime drift and dependency fragility
Containerized workloadsKubernetes apps with portable images, separated PVs, standard registriesStateless layers easy to move, stateful parts manageable with storage planK8s workloads with tangled storage, old CSI bindings, hidden infra dependenciesPV portability and platform coupling issues
File/content platformsShared content repos, NFS-backed app content, object-compatible app dataCan be copied/synced and repointedApps with business logic tightly coupled to local filesystem layoutsHardcoded mounts and path assumptions
ERP/CRM/custom LOB on supported stackSupported OS + supported DB + normal app/data separationCan often be stabilized on FLEX firstOld ERP/CRM on obsolete OS or vendor stack with no clean export pathBetter treated as replacement/replatform project
Analytics / reporting appsModern BI/reporting apps using supported DBs and standard app hostsOften portable if data sources are reachableOld report servers with brittle dependencies and low business valueUsually better to retire or archive
Batch / worker tiersETL jobs, schedulers, queue workers on supported OSEasy to relocate if dependencies are documentedCron-heavy legacy boxes with undocumented local scripts and old runtimesHidden operational logic and local-state risk
Customer-built appsModern custom apps using standard stacks and supported OSBest candidates for phased migrationDeeply customized legacy monolithsNeed refactor/replatform, not simple move
Appliance-like stacksFew, unless virtual appliance is vendor-supported on KVM/FLEXPossible only with explicit supportXen-dependent virtual appliances, proprietary clusters, special kernel appliancesHypervisor dependency or vendor lock-in
Mainframe / proprietary coreDownstream integration to FLEX data onlyFLEX can host replicas, feeds, analyticsMainframe DBs, RAC appliances, proprietary hardware platformsRetain in place, integrate rather than move

Nginx + Flask + PostgreSQLXen-dependent appliance or proprietary virtual machine

Stage 1 — Discovery & Assessment

Collect a full picture of the current OSPC environment before any migration work begins. The outputs of this stage feed directly into Stage 2.

📋 Tasks

  • Collect environment inventory – Gather details of all accounts, instances, images, volumes, and security groups.
  • Identify storage backend (Cinder) – Determine the storage technology in use to plan the appropriate migration approach.
  • Identify networking configuration & segmentation – ServiceNet, PublicNet, or Private Neutron Network.
  • Review quotas and utilisation – Evaluate current resource quotas and usage to properly size the Flex environment.
  • Identify unsupported features – Detect features/configurations not supported in Flex that require remediation before migration.

📦 Deliverables

  • Environment inventory – Detailed record of existing infrastructure (instances, storage, networking, security).
  • Capacity plan – Assessment of resource requirements to ensure Flex can support migrated workloads.
  • Migration risk assessment – Identification of potential risks, limitations, or unsupported features impacting migration.

☸️ Kubernetes Dual-Layer Scanner

        
Discover and map Kubernetes clusters to their underlying OpenStack compute and storage dependencies before migration.


        

          
Run Automated K8s & OSPC Dual-Scan

          
Paste your kubeconfig below or connect to the Bastion node to automatically map Kubernetes workloads to OpenStack VMs.

          
          
        


        
📚 Simplest Discovery Path by Tooling

        
The best file to get from the existing OSPC deployment relies entirely on how the cluster was built. Do not blindly copy VM nodes or disks.


        

          

            
1) Helm-Managed App (Highest Priority)

            
Export the app configuration and rendered YAML. The values.yaml is the single most reusable import path for Flex.

            
helm list -A
helm get values <release> -n <namespace> -a -o yaml > <release>-values.yaml
helm get manifest <release> -n <namespace> > <release>-manifest.yaml

          


          

            
2) Kustomize-Managed App

            
Download the entire repository folder containing the kustomization.yaml, base manifests, patches, and overlays.

          


          

            
3) Raw Kubernetes YAML (Source Repo)

            
If a Git repo exists without Helm/Kustomize, download all declarative objects: deployment.yaml, statefulset.yaml, service.yaml, ingress.yaml, configmap.yaml, pvc.yaml.

          


          

            
4) Live Cluster Export (Fallback Path)

            
If there is ZERO source repository, fallback to exporting exactly what is running on OSPC. Note: this YAML will be messy and contain runtime state strings.

            
kubectl get all,cm,secret,ingress,pvc,networkpolicy -A -o yaml > k8s-inventory-main.yaml
kubectl get storageclass,pv -o yaml > k8s-storage-export.yaml

          


          

            
Infrastructure Mapping Database

            
You MUST execute these to map Kubernetes to OpenStack Nova VMs and Cinder Storage.

            
kubectl get nodes -o wide
openstack server list --all-projects --long   # Map Internal K8s IPs to OSPC VM IDs
kubectl get pvc -A -o wide
openstack volume list --long   # Map Bound PVs to OpenStack Cinder Volume IDs

Performance

1B. User Profile & Target Permissions Matching (RBAC validation)

                        
Compare your assigned roles and permissions in OSPC against the new FLEX tenant to ensure no operational access was lost.


                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        Identity / RBAC area
                                        OSPC / legacy words
                                        FLEX words people use now
                                        What it really means
                                    

                                
                                
                                    

                                        Top business boundary
                                        Account
                                        Account + Domain
                                        FLEX still sits under a Rackspace account, but OpenStack identity structure adds the domain concept.
                                    

                                    

                                        Main resource ownership
                                        Tenant
                                        Project
                                        In practice, old "tenant" thinking maps to FLEX project thinking. FLEX UI/docs explicitly surface project and domain.
                                    

                                    

                                        Person who logs in
                                        User / cloud user
                                        User
                                        Same basic concept, but FLEX user access is more formally tied to project/domain permissions.
                                    

                                    

                                        Team of users
                                        List of users
                                        Group
                                        FLEX / Keystone makes groups a clearer identity object for assigning access by team instead of one-by-one.
                                    

                                    

                                        What someone is allowed to do
                                        Permissions
                                        Permissions
                                        Same word exists, but FLEX docs emphasize explicit role/permission setup for users.
                                    

                                    

                                        Named privilege bundle
                                        "admin" / "read-only"
                                        Role
                                        FLEX uses more formal role-based language under Keystone/OpenStack.
                                    

                                    

                                        Access model
                                        Simpler account access model
                                        RBAC on user/group/role
                                        FLEX is more structured and closer to upstream OpenStack identity concepts.
                                    

                                    

                                        Auth secret for humans
                                        User+Pass / API creds
                                        Username + API key
                                        FLEX explicitly calls out username, API key, project, and domain.
                                    

                                    

                                        Auth secret for scripts/apps
                                        Reused user creds
                                        Application Credential
                                        FLEX supports standalone execution credentials instead of reusing human login secrets.
                                    

                                    

                                        Single sign-on
                                        SSO
                                        Federation
                                        FLEX/Rackspace supports identity federation to sign in with corporate credentials.
                                    

                                    

                                        Admin manager
                                        Account owner
                                        Account Administrator
                                        Account Admins manage users and platform permissions at the project level.
                                    

                                    

                                        Login Context
                                        Account/region/tenant
                                        Project + Domain + Region
                                        FLEX login and CLI context explicitly require both project and domain variables.
                                    

                                    

                                        Session proof
                                        Auth
                                        Token
                                        FLEX uses strictly token-based access headers behind the scenes via Keystone.
                                    

                                    

                                        Server login shell
                                        SSH key
                                        SSH keypair
                                        FLEX explicitly mandates OpenStack SSH Keypair objects for initial VM deployment access.

🔬 Internal UAT Tasks Reference

      
🔬 Internal UAT Tasks

      
    
        
  • Verify VM boot – Ensure VMs start successfully in Flex.
          
    openstack server list --project <project_id> -c Name -c Status | grep ACTIVE
    
        
    • 
        
  • Validate network connectivity – Confirm instances communicate as expected.
          
    ping -c 4 <flex_floating_ip>
    nc -zv <flex_private_ip> 22
    
        
    • 
        
  • Confirm storage accessibility – Verify volumes and storage resources are accessible.
          
    openstack volume list --project <project_id> -c Name -c Status
    ssh user@<flex_ip> 'df -h | grep /dev/vd'
    
        
    • 
      

      
👤 Customer UAT Tasks

      
    
        
  • Access confirmed – Customer confirmed access to the new Flex environment.
    • 
        
  • Confirm application functionality – Applications operating correctly after migration.
    • 
      

      
📊 Validation Matrix

      

        
Workload TypeInternal UATCustomer UAT

        
          
DatabasesService up, replication healthy, storage OK, backup worksQueries correct, app reads/writes correct, reports match

          
App tiersVM boots, services start, DNS resolves, storage mountsUsers log in, transactions succeed, integrations work

          
ContainersPods healthy, PVCs mount, ingress worksApp flow works, no missing data, no broken sessions

          
Legacy / MonolithBoot and services stableCore business workflow works exactly as expected

          
SaaS replacementImport / reconciliation completeUsers validate records, process flow, reports

          
Archive / RetainData readable, access controlledBusiness can retrieve required data

        
      

      
🛠 Automated Checking Commands

      

        

          
Databases (Service & Replication)

          
# MySQL Replication Status
ssh admin@<db_ip> 'mysql -e "SHOW SLAVE STATUS\\G" | grep "Running:"'

# PostgreSQL Replication
ssh postgres@<db_ip> 'psql -xc "select * from pg_stat_replication;"'

        

        

          
App Tiers (DNS & Services)

          
# Check DNS Resolution
dig @<flex_dns> +short <app_url>

# Verify Web Service HTTP 200
curl -I -s https://<app_url> | head -n 1

# Systemd Service Status
ssh user@<app_ip> 'systemctl is-active <service_name>'

        

        

          
Containers (Pod/PVC Health)

          
# Verify Kubernetes Workload Health
kubectl get pods,pvc,ingress -n <namespace>

4. Cutover Execution Cockpit

              
Guided step-by-step cutover — run after Cutover TEST passes

            

          

          

            
            
          

          

            
            
            
          

        

        


          
          

            

              📋
              How to run a cutover
            

            


              

                

                  1
                  Click Start Cutover
                

                
Starts the timer and activates the cockpit. Steps stay locked until you click this first.

              


              

                

                  2
                  Run steps — manual or auto
                

                
Manual: click each step button left-to-right. Auto Chain: toggle Auto Chain: ON (top-right) before Start — steps run automatically in sequence, each with a 3-second cancel window.

              


              

                

                  3
                  DB in scope? (Step 4)
                

                
If no DB migration, uncheck "DB in scope" in Step 4 to skip it without blocking the final decision.

              


              

                

                  4
                  Final decision unlocks
                

                
All steps pass → Cut over PASS turns green. Critical fail → Rollback turns red.

              


              

                

                  5
                  Evidence & sign-off
                

                
Add operator notes → Archive Evidence → Export Evidence Package for customer sign-off.

📦 Customer Migration Report Export

          Customer-facing evidence from Stages 1 through 4
        

        

          
Generate a customer-facing migration evidence report from discovery, migration, validation, cutover, and rollback artifacts.

          

            
Why
Customers need clear evidence of what was migrated, how it was migrated, what passed validation, what risks remain, and how rollback is handled.

            
When
Run this after Stage 3 validation and Stage 4 cutover planning, during Stage 5 stabilization and handover.

            
Where
Stage 5 — Stabilization & Handover.

            
By Who
Cloud Admin Team, Migration Lead, Project Manager, Customer Success, Managed Services, and Account Team.

            
How
Collect artifacts from Stages 1 to 4, generate JSON, Markdown, and HTML reports, then include the report in the final migration handover bundle.

Stage 8

        
IaC Backup, DR & Restore

        
Terraform + Ansible recovery pack

        
Capture the migrated tenant state as reusable Terraform and Ansible artifacts. Use this stage to export the recovery pack, validate restore readiness, and rebuild the tenant in the same region, another region, or another OpenStack-compatible cloud.

        
For GitOps/OpenCenter-based redeployments, publish the same recovery pack to the GitOps repository and continue in Stage 9 — GitOps & OpenCenter Modernization.

      


      

        
How this stage works

        

          
1. Backup source

          The IaC recovery pack is created from the Migration Output Bundle generated in Stage 5 — Stabilization & Handover. When you click Generate Bundle in Stage 5, the system writes a timestamped bundle directory for the active customer. The bundle includes tenant-iac-dr/, which contains Terraform environment stubs, Ansible inventory snippets, backup-policy.yaml, restore runbooks, metadata, and restore scope documentation. This is an infrastructure-definition backup. It does not include full VM disk images, application binaries, or database row dumps. Full scope details are recorded in tenant-iac-dr/dr/BACKUP_SCOPE.md.

          
2. Backup export and publishing

          After Stage 5 succeeds, the dashboard keeps the latest bundle stamp for the session. Use Export IaC Backup to copy tenant-iac-dr/ into a configured Git working tree and/or upload backup archives to object storage.

          
Supported environment variables:

          
    
            
  • IAC_BACKUP_GIT_REPO_PATH
    • 
            
  • GITOPS_REPO_PATH
    • 
            
  • IAC_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET
    • 
            
  • GITOPS_PUSH_AFTER_COMMIT
    • 
          

          
3. Restore execution

          Restore consumes the same tenant-iac-dr/ recovery pack. Save the Target Cloud Profile, confirm the readiness banner shows that the Stage 5 bundle includes tenant-iac-dr/, then choose one restore path:

          
Option A — Direct Terraform / OpenStack Restore — same-region, cross-region, or cross-cloud OpenStack rebuilds without OpenCenter lifecycle automation.

          
Option B — GitOps / OpenCenter Restore Preparation — publish the recovery pack into GitOps and prepare OpenCenter-oriented restore stubs for repo-driven reconciliation.

          
4. Missing bundle recovery

          If preflight says the bundle is missing, return to Stage 5, select the same customer, run Generate Bundle again, then reopen Stage 7.

      Stage 9
      
        
      GitOps & OpenCenter Modernization
      
        
      Consume the Stage 7 recovery pack: publish backup/restore artifacts, create restore stubs, and drive repeatable redeploy pipelines in another FLEX region or OpenStack cloud.
      
      
      

      
      
        
      Import R6 Containerization Outputs
      
        
      R6 Containerization Bundle → OpenCenter Import → GitOps Repository → Flux Reconcile → Production Kubernetes Platform
      
        
      Import containerized application artifacts, Helm/Kustomize packaging, image plans, CI/CD metadata, and GitOps handoff files generated by R6 before deploying into OpenCenter. OpenCenter does not refactor the application. It runs the production Kubernetes/GitOps platform.
      
        
      
          
          
          
        
      
      
      

      
      
        
      Enable GitOps on your repo
      
        
      After push-backup, each bundle includes gitops-flux-stub/kustomization.yaml (empty Kustomize root) so Flux or Argo can use path: immediately. Generate YAML below, apply to the cluster, then extend the stub directory in Git with real resources.
      
        
      
          
          
          
          
        
      
        
      API: GET /api/gitops/register-snippets?customer=&stamp=&git_url=&branch=&flux_namespace=. Default git_url from GITOPS_PUBLIC_REPO_URL. Repo templates: gitops/templates/ in this project.
      
        
      
        
      
          
          
          
        
      
        
      
          
      Click “Generate Flux / Argo snippets” (requires a Stage 5 bundle for the active customer).

      Autorepair Intelligence
      Failed boot, network, service, and dependency signals become repair plans with risk and rollback notes.
      
        
      Optimization Loop
      Right-size flavors, improve Terraform/Ansible, and refine IAC DR runbooks after each wave.
      
      
      
    
      
  
      

  
  
      
    
      
      
      
        
      Stage 10
      
        
      AIOps & Continuous Operations
      
        
      AIOps consumes Cloud Jumper, FinOps, IaC, and GitOps / OpenCenter outputs to produce optimization and autorepair recommendations backed by GitOps-ready artifacts.
      
      
      
      
      
        
      Optimization
      Right-size recommendations, capacity tuning, and infra patch proposals.
      
        
      Autorepair
      Boot, network, service, and runbook remediation plans with rollback hints.
      
        
      GitOps Delivery
      Publish AIOps outputs as reviewable change candidates for GitOps pipelines.
